t: For expenses necessary to carry out the purposes of the Act relating to neurology and blindness, $128,934,500.

fable.w: This is a bare appropriation of funds for neurology and blindness programs. There is no tempting reading: it mentions no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government is involved in any federal decision.
fable.s: For expenses necessary to carry out the purposes of the Act relating to neurology and blindness, $128,934,500.

qwen_block.w: This section is a simple appropriation clause authorizing a specific amount of funding for certain purposes. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. It merely allocates funds.
qwen_block.s: For expenses necessary to carry out the purposes of the Act relating to neurology and blindness, $128,934,500.

opus.w: This section only funds expenses for the Act on neurology and blindness. It does not involve anyone outside the federal government in a federal decision. Mentioning another Act does not create participation, because nothing here requires or allows consultation, hearings, rulemaking or advisory input.
opus.b: The obvious wrong reading would be to treat a reference to "the Act" as bringing in whatever processes that Act sets up. That doesn't work: this section only provides money. It names no outside party and no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a simple appropriations clause authorizing a specific sum of money for certain purposes. It does not contain any language requiring or recommending consultation, coordination, public comment, hearings, or advisory committees involving parties outside the federal government. The mere authorization of funds does not constitute participation as defined.
qwen_chat.s: For expenses necessary to carry out the purposes of the Act relating to neurology and blindness, $128,934,500.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "expenses necessary to carry out the purposes of the Act" implies some process of engagement with beneficiaries or experts to determine those expenses. However, this is a standard appropriations clause that simply authorizes a specific amount of funding. It does not mandate any specific procedural interaction, consultation, hearing, or comment period with outside parties. The text is purely about budget authorization.
